item.content:encoded:
Bitcoin (BTC) slipped below $80,000 on Saturday as more than $200 million in crypto positions were liquidated within an hour. Traders betting on higher prices accounted for $191.33 million of that total.

Ethereum (ETH) fell alongside the leading crypto. BeInCrypto Markets data shows the total crypto market cap down 4.06% over the past 24 hours, at $2.72 trillion. The liquidation data shows who absorbed most of the losses.

Bullish Traders Absorb the Heaviest Losses

The hourly wave formed part of a larger 24-hour total. Data from Coinglass shows $837.12 million in liquidations over that period, hitting 227,681 traders.

Long positions made up 82.8% of that figure, or $693.05 million. Short sellers lost $144.07 million.

Bitcoin led the tally with $232.55 million, followed by Ethereum at $181.51 million. Longs accounted for more than 93% of each.

Binance recorded the largest single liquidation, an $11.85 million long on the ETHUSDT pair. Price data shows how far the sell-off reached beyond derivatives.

Follow us on X to get the latest news as it happens

Bitcoin Slips Under the Price Corporate Treasuries Paid

Bitcoin traded at $79,464 at press time, down 2.48% over 24 hours. This marked its lowest level since September 18.

Altcoins fell harder. Ethereum lost 4.71% over the same period to $2,288.73, its lowest level in about two months. Solana (SOL) dropped 5.20% to $98.92.

Zcash (ZEC) posted the steepest decline in the top 10, sliding 8.39% to $1,124.36.

Bitcoin now sits below $80,000, the average price that companies holding Bitcoin on their balance sheets paid per coin, according to Glassnode estimates. That puts the average corporate treasury position at a loss.

Earlier on Saturday, analyst Benjamin Cowen warned that a weekly close below $83,000 on October 25 would support his bearish path. He said the scenario becomes void if Bitcoin climbs back above $83,000 and holds there.

BeInCrypto’s analysis flagged $77,876 as the next downside level. Below that, a support zone sits between roughly $76,700 and $72,500.

The market has tested similar ground this month. On October 8, total crypto market cap fell to $2.69 trillion before a Trump pledge on Iran eased the pressure. Today’s $2.72 trillion sits about 1% above that floor.

Next week brings more tests. The Federal Reserve meets on October 27 and 28, and September Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation data follows on October 29.

Brent crude also settled at $116.72 on Friday, a level that could keep inflation elevated. Whether buyers defend $77,876 before those events could decide how much room Bitcoin has left.

The post Bitcoin Keeps Reversing. Why Are 80% of Crypto Tokens Falling? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Bitcoin has spent October making both bulls and bears look foolish. It slipped below $80,000 last week, recovered toward $84,000 this week, then fell back toward $81,000.

Each bounce has looked promising. Each reversal has exposed how little confidence there is behind it.

The damage is much worse beneath Bitcoin’s price. In its October 17–23 Token Pulse report, Bitunix found that roughly 80% of the 300 largest tokens it tracks lost value.

Their median weekly return was −3.98%, compared with Bitcoin’s relatively modest 0.71% decline. Cardano, NEAR and SUI lost more than 5%. Starknet’s STRK plunged 39.2%.

An overall crypto market recovery becomes harder to sustain when most cryptocurrencies are still falling.

Why Does Bitcoin Keep Reversing Course?

Expectations for US interest rates have shifted repeatedly. Early-week comments about labor-market weakness encouraged hopes of further Federal Reserve cuts. Bitcoin rose as investors anticipated cheaper money.

Stronger economic data then challenged expectations for rapid easing, sending it lower again, according to Bitunix.

Institutional money has been equally unpredictable.

US spot Bitcoin ETFs attracted $526.7 million on October 19 and $524.8 million on October 21. The following day, $635.6 million flowed out. 

That represents a remarkable $1.16 billion swing in net flows between consecutive sessions.

The pressure extends beyond crypto.

In Bitunix’s weekly stock-contract review, Intel fell 10.52% and Micron declined 8.05%. On October 22, the Nasdaq lost 2.6% as investors questioned the enormous cost of the AI boom.

Bitcoin fell alongside technology shares as investors reduced their appetite for risk.

Oil complicates the outlook further. Brent gained 6.8% over Bitunix’s reporting period amid escalating Middle East tensions. More expensive energy could keep inflation elevated, making interest-rate cuts harder to justify.

Even the few crypto winners are struggling. Lighter’s LIT gained 12.19% over seven days, supported by stronger platform activity and plans to seek US derivatives registrations. Yet it dropped more than 11% in the final 24 hours.

Will Bitcoin Recover Before October Ends?

The next major test arrives almost immediately.

The Federal Reserve meets October 27–28, followed by the September core PCE inflation report on October 29.

Annual core PCE inflation stood at 3.0% in August, still above the Fed’s 2% target.

Cooler inflation or reassuring Fed guidance could help Bitcoin challenge 84,000–85,000 again.

Persistent inflation, further ETF withdrawals or another technology-stock selloff could bring $80,000 back into focus.

For now, repeated recoveries show buyers remain willing to step in near $80,000. The sharp reversals suggest they have yet to establish control.

October’s volatility reflects a market with buyers at lower prices, but limited confidence in a sustained rally.

The post Bitcoin Keeps Reversing. Why Are 80% of Crypto Tokens Falling? appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.content:encoded:
American Express (Amex) shares closed 3.62% lower on Friday. This came as a surprise, as the credit card giant exceeded Q3 profit estimates. 

The company also announced plans to cut about 5% of its 77,000 global workforce to prepare for AI. Amex is also taking a $336 million restructuring charge tied to the plan.

Amex Wants Fewer Layers Before It Hands Work to AI

Chief Financial Officer Christophe Le Caillec gave CNBC three reasons for the move.

  • To make Amex leaner
  • To make the company more agile
  • To prepare it for AI

He also explained why the job cuts have to come before the automation.

“You don’t want to automate processes that are not optimally structured. So what we’re doing here is to reduce layers and increase spans of controls, so that we can automate and take advantage of AI in the coming quarters and the coming years,”  Le Caillec said.

Amex is not the only lender cutting staff. A day earlier, Barclays confirmed it would cut 5,000 jobs, about 5% of its workforce, in a tech-driven cost push. 

Six of the biggest US banks also shed 15,000 employees while lifting first-quarter profits 18% to $47 billion.

At Amex, the restructuring also shows up in the profit forecast. The company is paying for it with part of the one-time gain.

Why Did Amex Stock Fall Despite Strong Earnings?

The problem was how the company achieved those profits.

Amex’s earnings per share rose 13%, but its underlying pretax profit grew just 1.6%. Much of the earnings growth came from a lower tax bill and share buybacks, rather than stronger business performance.

Revenue also missed Wall Street’s expectations.

Meanwhile, Amex raised its annual profit forecast, but the increase was largely driven by a one-time gain from selling a business stake. Excluding that gain and restructuring costs, its outlook improved only slightly.

For investors, the results suggested Amex’s underlying business was growing more slowly than its headline earnings implied.

That disappointment, combined with uncertainty around its AI restructuring plans and a broader market sell-off, likely contributed to Friday’s decline.

item.content:encoded:
Arthur Hayes has sold about $22.28 million in crypto from Maelstrom’s directional book. Hayes, the family office’s chief investment officer, confirmed the exit on X and plans to sit out the market.

The post is a shift from his tone earlier this month. On October 15, Hayes urged traders to go long Bitcoin (BTC) and Ethereum (ETH) and trade an eventual bailout.

What Arthur Hayes Sold, and Why He Says He Left

Lookonchain data shows his biggest sale was 6,400 ETH, worth $15.2 million. Hayes also sold 14 million Ethena (ENA) for $2.76 million and 323,000 Uniswap (UNI) for $2.24 million.

Smaller sales included 1.89 million Ether.fi (ETHFI) and stakes in Aerodrome Finance (AERO), Pendle (PENDLE), and Zama (ZAMA).

Hayes then confirmed the exit in a post, citing macro and geopolitical risks.

Did Hayes Sell at a Profit This Time?

Hayes says he took profits on ETH and ENA. Lookonchain valued his 6,400 ETH at $15.2 million, or about $2,375 per coin, though his cost for those coins is not public. 

ENA offers a clearer comparison. In early August, he bought 9.05 million ENA for about $773,000, or roughly $0.085 per token.

Lookonchain valued Saturday’s ENA sale at about $0.20 per token. Still, it is unconfirmed whether the tokens sold are the same ones bought in August.

His newest bets fared worse. In mid-October, he bought Aerodrome, Pendle, and Zama tokens, Lookonchain reported.

He paid about $889,000 for them and sold them for about $856,000, based on Lookonchain’s prices at each trade. That leaves a loss of roughly $33,000.

The Slide Goes Beyond Hayes’ Tokens

His exit came during a broader market downturn. Six of the seven tokens he sold are down over the past month, according to BeInCrypto Markets.

The decline also puts Hayes’ earlier price targets in perspective. His September forecasts of $10,000 for ETH, $0.50 for ENA, and $2 for ETHFI remain well above current prices.

Broader market stress intensified this month. On October 15, crypto liquidations reached $942.1 million in 24 hours, with long positions accounting for 91.6% of the total.

On October 23, another selloff sent the Nasdaq down 2.6% and Bitcoin toward $81,400. Rising oil prices added to inflation concerns, putting monetary policy back in focus.

Why the Fed Is the Next Test

The Federal Reserve’s next decision, due October 28, could shape the outlook for risk assets. The Fed raised rates to 3.75%–4% on September 16, its first hike since July 2023. CME FedWatch data puts the odds of a hold at 90%.

The longer-term outlook remains uncertain. Minutes from September’s meeting showed most officials expected another hike by year-end. Hayes, by contrast, has argued that an eventual AI bailout would flood markets with new money.

His own trading history offers another reason to watch how he handles the latest exit. In August 2025, Hayes sold ETH near $3,507 and bought back nine days later at about $4,252.

A trader who copied the move would have paid roughly 21% more to reenter. For altcoin holders, the October 28 decision could help determine whether Hayes’ latest exit proves timely or premature.

item.description:

Analyst Benjamin Cowen warns that a weekly close below $83,000 on October 25 would strengthen his bearish outlook for the rest of 2026. His warning comes as Bitcoin faces pressure well beyond its

The post Bitcoin Faces Make-or-Break Weekend as Market Crash Fears Grow appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Bitcoin is approaching a make-or-break weekend. After failing to hold $83,000, the cryptocurrency is now facing a more uncomfortable level at $80,000.

Analyst Benjamin Cowen warns that a weekly close below $83,000 on October 25 would strengthen his bearish outlook for the rest of 2026. His warning comes as Bitcoin faces pressure well beyond its own price chart.

Why Bitcoin’s $80,000 Level Matters

The latest failed rally has already punished bullish traders. During one four-hour selloff, long positions accounted for $91.19 million of $95.22 million in crypto liquidations.

More concerning, Glassnode estimates that companies holding Bitcoin on their balance sheets paid about $80,000 per coin on average.

Falling below that level would put the average corporate treasury position into a loss. It would not automatically force companies to sell, but it could weaken confidence.

A separate BeInCrypto analysis identifies $77,876 as the next downside level if selling persists, followed by a support zone between roughly $76,700 and $72,500.

US spot Bitcoin ETFs also lost about $322 million on October 22, suggesting institutional buying has weakened.

What Happens to Bitcoin Next Week?

The calendar offers little relief. The Federal Reserve meets October 27–28, with Cowen expecting interest rates to stay unchanged. September inflation data follows on October 29.

Oil adds another complication. Brent settled at $116.72 on Friday as Middle East supply fears intensified. Expensive energy could keep inflation elevated, while rising Treasury yields make speculative investments less attractive.

History also gives bears ammunition. Binance Research puts Bitcoin’s average decline during previous US midterm election years at 56%. But that record covers only three Bitcoin cycles, making it a warning rather than a reliable prediction.

There is also a clear way for Bitcoin to break Cowen’s bearish scenario.

For now, the immediate test is whether buyers defend $80,000. A sustained recovery above $83,000 would weaken the bearish case.

Losing $80,000 could expose Bitcoin to another wave of selling just as November’s US midterm elections approach.

item.content:encoded:
Uniswap (UNI) has lost 25.75% of its value over the past month, sliding to $6.93. On-chain data, however, shows new users arriving at the fastest pace since November 2022.

Santiment counted 2,295 new UNI wallets in a single day. The firm said that influx could firm up a price base, provided wallet creation stays elevated.

Uniswap’s v4 Push Pulls In Fresh Wallets

Santiment’s network growth metric counts addresses interacting with UNI for the first time. The firm said a four-year high signals a large influx of new participants.

Santiment credited new Uniswap v4 features, wider liquidity routing, and ongoing work on Unichain, Uniswap’s layer-2 network.

DefiLlama data shows Uniswap v4 now holds about $1.44 billion in total value locked (TVL). That marks a roughly 17% rise over the past month.

So far, however, the activity has not stopped the token’s decline. UNI is down 3.82% over the past 24 hours, adding to its monthly losses, per BeInCrypto Markets data

Analyst Phoenix traced the decline to seller pressure after UNI tested the $10 mark. He noted the price has since dropped below the Ichimoku cloud and its moving averages on shrinking volume.

Phoenix warned that a full breakdown of $7 could send UNI toward $6 to $6.50. The token now sits just under that line at $6.93.

Santiment framed the same level in terms of user demand.

“Holding $7 while network growth remains above its recent baseline would favor another test of $8, while losing $7 alongside fading wallet creation would suggest the spike was mostly short-term excitement rather than sustained adoption,” the post read.

UNI Price Outlook

Winning back those losses starts with a move above $7. Santiment named $7.50 as the first meaningful level to reclaim, followed by $8.

On October 21, when UNI traded above $7, analyst Scient flagged bullish four-hour divergences. He floated a possible squeeze similar to Zcash’s (ZEC).

Analyst Defi Rocketeer finds the $7 area more interesting than the rally near $11. He expects a $10 to $12 retest if the broader market stabilizes. Analyst CryptoBullet places major resistance further up, at $13 to $15.

For holders, the next signals to watch are Santiment’s network growth readings and whether UNI can close above $7. A recovery in both would bring Santiment’s $8 test back into play.

item.content:encoded:
Swiss blue chips lead euro-area peers by almost 8 percentage points in October, the widest gap since March 2020.

The Swiss Market Index (SMI) is up 4.6% this month, and the Euro Stoxx 50 is down 3.2%. Bloomberg linked the gap to 3 forces pushing investors to cut risk in Europe.

  • Rising borrowing costs
  • Growing doubts about the AI trade
  • Political turmoil in France and Spain

3 Giants Carry the Swiss Lead

Investors in Europe have favored profitable companies with strong balance sheets, which are less exposed to rising borrowing costs. Bloomberg named the SMI one of the biggest beneficiaries of that shift, and its 3 largest companies produced the entire October gain.

Drugmaker Roche has climbed 12% in October, and rival Novartis has added 6.7%. Food group Nestlé has gained 10%.

Together, the 3 make up almost half the SMI’s value. Buying the index today is largely a bet on those 3 stocks.

Their run coincided with a global selloff in AI shares. CNBC said 20 of the top AI and chip stocks shed over $1 trillion from October 12 to 15.

Investors worried that higher borrowing costs could weigh on AI spending. Global corporate bond spreads have since widened to their highest since May 2025.

Damian Burkhardt of EFG Asset Management tied the Swiss gains to that retreat from AI.

“Investors like the defensiveness of Swiss stocks and are actively looking for alternatives to the crowded AI trades. Healthcare was the funding sector for the AI trade, and that is reversing now,” he said.

Bank of America’s global fund manager survey shows how crowded that trade was before the selloff.

Managers polled from October 2 to 8 held their largest tech allocation since August 2020. BofA’s separate European survey ranked Switzerland joint second at a net 16%, behind Spain’s net 28%.

The rally has also made Swiss shares pricier, which raises the question of how far it can run.

item.title: Global Economic Outlook 2027: Are We Heading Toward Another Financial Crisis?
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Shahid
item.description:

What’s more concerning is a combination of problems developing simultaneously. Individually, these problems are manageable. Together, they

The post Global Economic Outlook 2027: Are We Heading Toward Another Financial Crisis? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
The world economy is entering a dangerous period, but a Great Depression-style collapse is still a remote possibility. 

A prolonged economic slowdown, further stock-market corrections, and a potential recession in some major economies are much more credible risks.

What’s more concerning is a combination of problems developing simultaneously.

  • Wall Street is questioning whether the enormous investments in AI will generate sufficient profits. 
  • China’s domestic economy remains weak. 
  • The war in the Middle East has pushed oil prices above $117 a barrel. 
  • Inflation is proving stubborn, and governments have less financial flexibility to rescue their economies.

Individually, these problems are manageable. Together, they increase the possibility of a more serious downturn.

What the Latest Economic Data Tells Us

There’s an important distinction between a financial-market crash and an economic crisis. Stocks can fall 30% without producing a global depression. 

The situation becomes much more dangerous when declining asset prices trigger defaults, reduce lending, and cause businesses to cut investment and jobs.

We have evidence of the first stage, but it’s much weaker for a worldwide economic breakdown.

However, these forecasts rely on assumptions about energy supplies, financial conditions, and investment that could deteriorate. The IMF’s projections were based on information available through October 1, before the latest market turmoil.

The biggest concern is that the global economy has become unusually dependent on a few sources of growth while its traditional economic safety mechanisms are under pressure.

AI Economy is the Biggest Risk of 2027

AI spending has become a significant contributor to investment growth in the United States. It has also supported exports from Asian chipmakers and generated orders for companies building data centers.

A serious reduction in AI spending would affect a much wider set of industries than technology shares.

The problem is the interconnected financing.

An AI company may receive money from a technology investor and then commit to buying computing services from that investor. Those promised future purchases help justify further infrastructure spending and borrowing.

If the AI company’s revenue disappoints, multiple businesses can suffer simultaneously. The investor’s stake loses value, future service revenue becomes uncertain, and creditors become concerned about repayment.

The IMF explicitly identifies this interconnected financing as a potential channel for wider financial stress.

The most frightening economic scenario is a sequence of AI infrastructure bankruptcies followed by widespread cancellations of data-center projects. That would indicate that the decline had moved beyond stock valuations.

So far, evidence of that industry-wide collapse is lacking.

Oil and Inflation are at the Heart of All Financial Nightmare

The second major risk is the Middle East conflict.

Brent crude reached approximately $116–117 on October 23, while the US 10-year Treasury yield was around 5%.

These two figures create an uncomfortable situation for central banks.

Consider what happens if businesses begin losing customers and unemployment rises.

Ordinarily, a central bank could respond by reducing interest rates. Cheaper financing would help households and businesses.

But if oil prices remain high, inflation may remain elevated. Cutting interest rates aggressively could then intensify inflationary pressures.

In its October forecast, the IMF estimated that a prolonged Middle East conflict keeping oil above $130 through the first quarter of 2027 could reduce next year’s global growth rate by around 0.5 percentage points.

Can China Trigger a Worldwide Recession?

China’s economic problems are important because it is one of the world’s largest manufacturing economies and a major consumer of raw materials.

Its property crisis has reduced household confidence. Weak spending is holding back business revenue, and companies have been cutting prices to compete for customers.

There are two possible international spillovers.

First, a slowdown in Chinese imports. If China’s construction and manufacturing sectors reduce their purchases, commodity producers and exporters elsewhere may suffer.

Second, more intense export competition. Chinese manufacturers facing weak domestic demand may seek more customers overseas. 

Cheaper goods could help contain inflation in importing countries, while putting pressure on competing manufacturers and increasing trade tensions.

China’s situation is a persistent drag on world growth. A more dangerous scenario would involve disorderly failures at major financial institutions or a sudden deterioration in credit availability.

China still has substantial state control over its banking system and capacity to intervene, which can reduce immediate financial contagion. 

That does not eliminate the cost of prolonged economic weakness.

We Might Not See Another Great Depression, Yet

There are several important signs that the financial system is still functioning.

  • US unemployment remains relatively low. The September unemployment rate was 4.2%. Hiring is weak, with just 29,000 jobs added, but we have not yet seen the widespread layoffs characteristic of a major economic crisis.
  • New unemployment claims remain contained. Weekly initial claims fell to 194,000 in the latest report, the lowest level in three months.
  • Broad corporate credit markets are functioning. US high-yield corporate credit spreads were around 3.27 percentage points on October 21. By comparison, they reached almost 20 points during the 2008 credit crisis. Today’s figure does not indicate a comparable system-wide credit freeze.

The IMF also describes the global banking system as broadly resilient, although it warns of vulnerabilities in private credit and highly leveraged investment strategies.

The important comparison is therefore closer to the early-2000s technology correction, with additional energy and sovereign-debt risks.

A 2008-style crisis would become more plausible if the losses spread through credit markets, major lenders became distressed and access to financing deteriorated sharply.

A 1930s-style depression would require an even more severe and prolonged breakdown in economic activity.

Neither is established by the market evidence available today.

4 Possible Outcomes for 2027

A broader analysis can divide the next 12–18 months into four scenarios.

These probability estimates are my subjective assessment of the current evidence. They are not outputs from a calibrated forecasting model.

Most Likely: Painful Market Correction, Continued Economic Growth

Technology stocks experience further repricing. AI investment growth slows, oil eventually stabilizes and the world economy continues expanding unevenly.

Stock markets remain volatile, although diversified investors may see recoveries before economic data noticeably improves.

Material Downside Risk: Stagflation and Regional Recessions

High energy prices persist. Consumer spending weakens and businesses reduce investment. One or more major economies enter recession, while global growth remains weak but positive.

Equities could enter a prolonged bear market, and central banks have limited flexibility to stimulate growth.

Severe Downside: Synchronized Global Recession and Financial Stress

AI investment declines sharply, defaults spread through vulnerable borrowers and financial institutions restrict lending. Higher unemployment and falling demand reinforce each other across major economies.

This would resemble aspects of 2008, with substantial losses across risky assets.

What Does This Mean for Crypto Markets?

Crypto investors should pay particular attention because their portfolios can be highly exposed to changes in global liquidity.

Bitcoin was trading around $82,000 on October 23. US spot Bitcoin ETFs experienced approximately $636 million in net outflows on October 22, following three days of strong inflows.

Institutional digital-asset platform Talos estimated Bitcoin’s 30-day correlation with the Nasdaq at around 0.6 on October 22. That indicates meaningful positive co-movement recently, though the relationship changes over time.

The important point is that Bitcoin cannot be assumed to protect a portfolio during an immediate financial panic.

An asset can have a long-term scarcity thesis and still fall sharply when investors urgently need liquidity.

Traders should be particularly cautious about altcoins going into 2027. Many have weaker liquidity and depend heavily on speculative demand. Some may not recover even if Bitcoin eventually reaches new highs.

There is a possible positive development for crypto further ahead. If inflation falls enough for central banks to ease monetary policy while financial stability is preserved, Bitcoin could benefit from improved liquidity.

But aggressive rate cuts during a financial crisis would not necessarily produce an immediate crypto rally. Forced selling often comes first.

5 Warning Signs to Monitor in 2027

These are monitoring thresholds, not precise recession triggers.

If oil prices decline, credit markets remain stable and corporate earnings hold up, the global outlook could improve substantially.

The post Oil Price Nears Yearly High: Is a Stock and Crypto Crash Coming?  appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Oil is climbing toward its yearly high, and the timing could hardly be worse for financial markets. Wall Street is already struggling, Bitcoin has fallen sharply, and investors now face another threat: a renewed US war with Iran after the midterm elections.

Brent crude touched $117.42 per barrel on Friday, October 23, its highest since April. Here are the latest catalysts: 

  • The immediate trigger was fresh attacks by Iran-backed Houthi forces on Saudi Arabia. 
  • Saudi Aramco evacuated its headquarters as fighting intensified. 
  • An oil spill near the United Arab Emirates added to concerns about shipping security.
  • The bigger concern comes from Washington. The US and Israel have reportedly prepared plans for renewed strikes against Iran, potentially targeting energy infrastructure after the November 3 elections.

The White House says no attack will happen before the vote. Military planning does not guarantee strikes will follow.

Why Are Stocks and Bitcoin Falling?

Thursday offered a warning. The Nasdaq plunged 2.6%, while the S&P 500 lost 1.2%. Bitcoin dropped toward $81,400 as crypto liquidations approached $441 million.

Concerns over enormous AI spending triggered much of the technology selloff. Rising oil prices added another problem.

More expensive energy pushes inflation higher, potentially forcing the Federal Reserve to maintain restrictive interest rates. That threatens corporate earnings and makes speculative assets such as Bitcoin less attractive.

Friday’s reaction remained mixed, with the Nasdaq recovering slightly while the Dow declined.

Will the Midterms Bring Another Market Crash?

History offers some reassurance. According to MSCI, US stocks gained an average of 12% in the six months following the past 13 midterm elections.

However, this year’s biggest uncertainty could emerge after voting ends.

Renewed strikes against Iran could push oil beyond $120 and toward its yearly peak, raising the risk of another inflation-driven selloff. De-escalation could ease oil prices and support a recovery.

For now, the next direction of stocks and crypto may depend more on what happens in the Middle East than who wins Congress.

item.dc:creator: Harsh Notariya
item.description:
BTCC, the world’s longest-serving cryptocurrency exchange, today released its Q3 2026 Growth Report, highlighting the flagship 0-Barrier Trading theme translating into record total futures volume, a sixfold increase in TradFi volume, and $121 million saved for traders. $387 Billion in Futures Volume, With a $16.7 Billion Peak Day BTCC’s futures trading volume reached $387 billion

The post BTCC Exchange Q3 2026 Growth Report: 0-Barrier Trading Powers a $387B Quarter, With TradFi Volume Up 6x to $16.3B appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
BTCC, the world’s longest-serving cryptocurrency exchange, today released its Q3 2026 Growth Report, highlighting the flagship 0-Barrier Trading theme translating into record total futures volume, a sixfold increase in TradFi volume, and $121 million saved for traders.

$387 Billion in Futures Volume, With a $16.7 Billion Peak Day

BTCC’s futures trading volume reached $387 billion in Q3, up 32% quarter-on-quarter. The highest-volume day was August 21, 2026, when single-day volume hit $16.7 billion as Bitcoin began its rally in late August.

The momentum extended well beyond crypto. TradFi volume rose from $2.7 billion in Q2 to $16.3 billion. BTCC also launched USDC-margined trading pairs covering popular crypto like BTC and DOGE, as well as stocks such as SKHYNIX and MRNA. 

BTCC’s user base also grew to 12.6 million, as more traders came to trade crypto and traditional markets on a single platform.

Helping Users Save $121 Million in Fees & Coverage

Alongside the growth in volume, BTCC worked to lower the cost of trading: in Q3, zero-fee pairs and first-trade loss coverage together delivered $121 million in value to traders:

  • $56 million in fees saved through zero-fee pairs.
  • $65 million in first futures trade loss coverage, giving eligible users up to 50 USDT each when their first futures trade ends in a loss.

PoR Above 100% at All Times and Refreshed Trust Center

Lower costs are only part of the 0-barrier promise; traders also need confidence that their assets are protected. To that end, BTCC added $2.5 million to its Risk Reserve Fund, bringing the total to $28 million in Q3. The fund is designed to provide additional protection for user assets in the event of unexpected market conditions.

BTCC’s Proof of Reserves is also maintained above 100% at all times. In October 2026, the Merkle tree-verified report shows that the total PoR is 132% and that all major cryptos are over-collateralized: 

  • BTC: 147%
  • ETH: 123%
  • XRP: 136%
  • USDT: 115%
  • USDC: 111%
  • ADA: 160%

Alongside these figures, BTCC launched its refreshed Trust Center, bringing its security measures, financial protections and transparency commitments into one place, from multi-signature cold storage and 24/7 AML controls to independent security audits by CertiK.

0-Barrier Trading Takes the Stage at TOKEN2049 Singapore

BTCC took the same message to its community in person at TOKEN2049 Singapore. As Platinum Sponsor, the exchange brought its 0-Barrier Trading theme to Marina Bay Sands, built around four pillars: 0 Fees, 0 Friction, 0 Distance and 0 Panic, which stand for lower costs, smoother trading, native-language support and security that users can verify.

“TOKEN2049 Singapore gave us the chance to put faces to the community we’ve been building for 15 years. It reinforced something we believe at BTCC: trust is earned one trader at a time, through consistency, transparency and a platform that puts users first,” said Alex Hung, Head of Operations at BTCC.

In Q2, BTCC named 0-Barrier Trading as its next chapter. In Q3, it became something traders could see, use and verify. Heading into the final quarter of its 15th anniversary year, BTCC will continue to build toward trading with zero barriers.

About BTCC

Founded in 2011, BTCC is a leading global cryptocurrency exchange serving over 12.6 million users across 100+ countries. As the official regional sponsor of the Argentine Football Association (AFA), BTCC offers secure and accessible cryptocurrency trading services, focused on delivering a user-friendly experience while adhering to applicable regulatory standards.

Official website: https://www.btcc.com/en-US

X: https://x.com/BTCCexchange

item.content:encoded:
FM Summit London will hold its 15th edition on Nov. 24 at Old Billingsgate in London, and registration is now open. The one-day event brings together professionals from online trading, institutional finance, brokerage, liquidity, trading technology, fintech, payments and digital assets.

Alongside a conference programme, the event will feature an exhibition where sponsors and exhibitors can showcase their solutions and meet potential clients. 

Confirmed exhibitors include LMAX Group, Plus500, oneZero, PLUGIT, Adaptive, ATFX, CMC Markets, MetaQuotes, Devexperts, Finalto, Edge Hound, AEGIS Trading Technology, Acuity and CXM Prime. Through the Business Connect program, attendees can also book pre-arranged one-to-one meetings and join invitation-only roundtables.

Opening Networking Blitz on Nov. 23

The event opens a day early with the Opening Networking Blitz on Nov. 23 at The Folly, in London. This pre-event gathering gives attendees a chance to meet peers and potential partners ahead of the main summit.

Speaker Hall

The Speaker Hall program includes a fireside chat with Lord Peter Cruddas, founder and CEO of CMC Markets, on his career, the evolution of retail trading and the industry’s future.

Other speakers include:

  • Hormoz Faryar, Managing Director of Institutional Sales, ATFX Connect, MEA
  • Andy Ross, Head of Institutional, Kalshi
  • Waqar Chaudry, Managing Director, Global Head of Digital Assets, Standard Chartered Bank

Business Connect Roundtables

The Business Connect Roundtables are invitation-only discussions led by experienced chairs. Topics include digital assets, prediction markets, market liquidity, payments and stablecoins, AI for traders and brokers, the future of funded firms, the UK’s role in retail trading, marketing and answer engine optimization (AEO), offshore versus onshore licensing, and tokenization.

Participation is subject to an invitation and selection process.

Registration Passes

FM Summit London offers three pass options:

  • P1 — Brokers & Prop Firms: free for eligible professionals.
  • P2 — Affiliates & IBs: free for eligible affiliates, introducing brokers and qualifying industry professionals.
  • P3 — Banks & Service Providers: paid pass for eligible banks, payment providers, technology providers and service providers. 

Eligibility terms and pricing are listed on the FM Summit London registration page.

More information is available on the FM Summit London website.

item.title: Why Did Copper Fall After a 44% Shortage Warning?
item.dc:creator: Jakub Dziadkowiec
item.description:
Copper breaks its April trendline as BloombergNEF projects a 44% supply deficit by 2050. See the key levels to watch.

The post Why Did Copper Fall After a 44% Shortage Warning? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Copper fell 2.68% on October 22, breaking an April support trendline that had held through five tests. The drop came two days after BloombergNEF warned of a copper supply deficit reaching 44% of demand by 2050.

Yet the same report rates the 2026 copper market in surplus. Traders appear to be pricing that near-term cushion, not the long-term gap.

Why Is Copper the Odd One Out?

BloombergNEF (BNEF) published its annual Transition Metals Outlook on October 20. Nine of the 10 materials it covers should have enough supply through 2050.

Copper is the exception. BNEF projects a 20 million tonne shortfall by 2050, starting as early as 2028.

Demand is set to climb 61% to nearly 46 million tonnes a year. Electrified transport alone accounts for 11.4 million.

Closing the gap would take $332 billion in new mines. Each one needs about 17 years to start producing, according to BNEF.

Martin Tengler, BNEF’s head of metals and mining, framed it as a timing problem.

“The challenge now is less about whether the world can produce enough metals overall, and more about whether the right materials will be available when and where they are needed.”

The metal exists. The US Geological Survey (USGS) puts global reserves near 980 million tonnes.

Why Did Copper Fall Anyway?

BNEF’s own scorecard also holds a sideways 12-month price view for copper.

Physical flows agree. London Metal Exchange (LME) copper stocks rose to 272,950 tonnes, the highest since July 24, Reuters reported.

Most new metal landed in US warehouses. Comex, the main US futures exchange, slipped to a discount against the LME, erasing its tariff-driven premium.

Alastair Munro, senior metals strategist at broker Marex, linked the two.

“…the recent build in LME copper stocks was the result of the COMEX premium shrinking as contract delivery dates draw closer.”

A tech-stock selloff over AI doubts added pressure, dragging LME copper to a five-week low.

Copper Supply Deficit: What’s Next for XCU Price?

The breakdown confirms the risk flagged during copper’s fifth support test this week.

The trendline formed the base of a rising wedge, a pattern that often resolves lower. Volume also rose on the break.

Meanwhile, copper was rejected near $6.70 resistance. The Relative Strength Index (RSI), a momentum gauge, lost a support line dating to March.

Copper now trades near $6.51 per pound, about 6% below its September record high. Resistance sits at $6.56, then at the broken trendline near $6.64.

On the downside, the 0.382 Fibonacci level at $6.31 could be the first target. Deeper supports lie at $6.11 and $5.91.

However, a daily close back above the trendline would weaken the bearish setup.

For now, copper trades on today’s surplus rather than the 2028 deficit. The bigger question is whether $332 billion in new mines arrives in time.
